organism.compatibilityNote: The primary chapter names Aspergillus niger 10 and includes the ORSTOM laboratory in the author affiliations, but its microorganism methods do not repeat the var. hennebergi / ORSTOM-collection wording from the Larralde-Corona pack. Preserve this as an explicit same-named-strain context transfer rather than silently treating the chapter label alone as an exact taxonomic join.

sources.note: The 1998 article abstract reports a broader initial-glucose range and complete-consumption boundary. Do not merge its summarized rows numerically with the 1997 chapter table unless exact row equivalence is verified.

agarSurfaceContext.inoculationLimitation: The accessible primary chapter text does not give enough inoculation-geometry/starting-biomass detail to equate this surface-culture setup with the current central-point fungal runtime.

biomass.method: Agar medium and biomass removed from the dish; agar dissolved in hot distilled water; suspension filtered and solids washed; total biomass determined by dry weight at 60 C.

sourceNarrativeChecks.tableVsNarrativeNote: The source table reports 96% substrate conversion at 100 g/L while the prose describes complete utilization within 70 h. Preserve both statements as a source-level rounding/summary discrepancy; do not coerce 96% to 100% in machine authority.

runtimeDecision.reason: The chapter supplies source-context endpoint/summary yield and conversion rows, but no zero-glucose row, no exact tabulated glucose-consumption time series/rate law, no transferable local transport coefficient, and no evidence that source-reported aggregate Yx/s is a constant instantaneous uptake law. The current fungal runtime also has front radius rather than a source-backed biomass state, so coupling glucose depletion to front advance would require an unsourced biomass mapping.

validationHandoff.nextEvidenceNeed: An exact no.10-compatible zero-resource/near-zero control and a source-backed or explicitly calibrated biomass/resource state law (or exact tabulated time-course data sufficient to fit one) are required before #615/#895 may activate a resource-coupled runtime.
